xcsh/21.11.8
xcsh v21.11.8

USAGE
  $ xcsh [COMMAND]

ARGUMENTS
  MESSAGES   Messages to send (prefix files with @)

FLAGS
      --model=<value>                 Model to use (fuzzy match: "opus", "gpt-5.2", or "p-openai/gpt-5.2")
      --smol=<value>                  Smol/fast model for lightweight tasks (or PI_SMOL_MODEL env)
      --slow=<value>                  Slow/reasoning model for thorough analysis (or PI_SLOW_MODEL env)
      --plan=<value>                  Plan model for architectural planning (or PI_PLAN_MODEL env)
      --provider=<value>              Provider to use (legacy; prefer --model)
      --context=<value>               Bind this session to a named F5 XC context
      --api-key=<value>               API key (defaults to env vars)
      --system-prompt=<value>         System prompt (default: coding assistant prompt)
      --append-system-prompt=<value>  Append text or file contents to the system prompt
      --allow-home                    Allow starting in ~ without auto-switching to a temp dir
      --no-sandbox                    Disable the session filesystem discovery guard
      --allow-path=<value>            Allow directory discovery at an additional path (repeatable)
      --mode=<value>                  Output mode: text (default), json, rpc, or acp
  -p, --print                         Non-interactive mode: process prompt and exit
  -c, --continue                      Continue previous session
  -r, --resume=<value>                Resume a session (by ID prefix, path, or picker if omitted)
      --fork=<value>                  Fork an existing session by ID prefix or path
      --session-dir=<value>           Directory for session storage and lookup
      --no-session                    Don't save session (ephemeral)
      --no-memories                   Disable project memory loading and maintenance
      --models=<value>                Comma-separated model patterns for Ctrl+P cycling
      --no-tools                      Disable all built-in tools
      --no-mcp                        Disable MCP server discovery and tools
      --no-lsp                        Disable LSP tools, formatting, and diagnostics
      --no-pty                        Disable PTY-based interactive bash execution
      --tools=<value>                 Comma-separated list of tools to enable (default: all)
      --thinking=<value>              Set thinking level: minimal, low, medium, high, xhigh, max
      --hook=<value>                  Load a hook/extension file (can be used multiple times)
  -e, --extension=<value>             Load an extension file (can be used multiple times)
      --plugin-dir=<value>            Load plugin from directory (repeatable)
      --no-extensions                 Disable extension discovery (explicit -e paths still work)
      --no-skills                     Disable skills discovery and loading
      --skills=<value>                Comma-separated glob patterns to filter skills (e.g., git-*,docker)
      --no-rules                      Disable rules discovery and loading
      --export=<value>                Export session file to HTML and exit
      --list-models=<value>           List available models (with optional fuzzy search)
      --no-title                      Disable title auto-generation

EXAMPLES
  # Interactive mode
    xcsh
  # Interactive mode with initial prompt
    xcsh "List all .ts files in src/"
  # Include files in initial message
    xcsh @prompt.md @image.png "What color is the sky?"
  # Non-interactive mode (process and exit)
    xcsh -p "List all .ts files in src/"
  # Continue previous session
    xcsh --continue "What did we discuss?"
  # Use different model (fuzzy matching)
    xcsh --model opus "Help me refactor this code"
  # Limit model cycling to specific models
    xcsh --models claude-sonnet,claude-haiku,gpt-4o
  # Export a session file to HTML
    xcsh --export ~/.xcsh/agent/sessions/--path--/session.jsonl

COMMANDS
  agents       Manage bundled task agents
  apply        Apply manifests by creating, updating, or preserving resources
  chrome       Inspect or arrange the Chrome session xcsh drives for console automation
  chrome-host  Native-messaging relay between Chrome and the xcsh manager socket (internal)
  commit       Generate a commit message and update changelogs
  config       Manage configuration settings
  create       Create resources from manifests and fail if they already exist
  delete       Delete resources identified by manifests or kind and name
  diff         Compare manifests with live resources without mutation
  export       Export live resources as manifests
  get          Get or list live resources
  grep         Test grep tool
  grievances   View reported tool issues (auto-QA grievances)
  herdr        Launch xcsh in a conversation-owned Herdr workspace
  jupyter      Manage the shared Jupyter gateway
  manager      Run the detached control server that spawns/reaps per-tab workers; blocks forever
  office       Serve, print, or sideload the embedded xcsh Office task pane
  plugin       Manage plugins (install, uninstall, list, etc.)
  read         Read a file as a chunk tree
  sandbox      Verify the installed filesystem sandbox
  search       Test web search providers
  self-update  Check for and install xcsh executable updates
  setup        Install dependencies for optional features
  shell        Interactive shell console
  ssh          Manage SSH host configurations
  stats        View usage statistics
  update       Update the xcsh executable or existing resources from manifests
  validate     Validate manifests locally without API credentials
  worker       Run a headless extension-bridge worker (no TUI); blocks until SIGTERM

Environment Variables:
  # Core Providers
  ANTHROPIC_API_KEY          - Anthropic Claude models
  ANTHROPIC_OAUTH_TOKEN      - Anthropic OAuth (takes precedence over API key)
  CLAUDE_CODE_USE_FOUNDRY    - Enable Anthropic Foundry mode (uses Foundry endpoint + mTLS)
  FOUNDRY_BASE_URL           - Anthropic Foundry base URL (e.g., https://<foundry-host>)
  ANTHROPIC_FOUNDRY_API_KEY  - Anthropic token used as Authorization: Bearer <token> in Foundry mode
  ANTHROPIC_CUSTOM_HEADERS   - Extra Foundry headers (e.g., "user-id: USERNAME")
  CLAUDE_CODE_CLIENT_CERT    - Client certificate (PEM path or inline PEM) for mTLS
  CLAUDE_CODE_CLIENT_KEY     - Client private key (PEM path or inline PEM) for mTLS
  NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS        - CA bundle path (or inline PEM) for server certificate validation
  OPENAI_API_KEY             - OpenAI GPT models
  GEMINI_API_KEY             - Google Gemini models
  GITHUB_TOKEN               - GitHub Copilot (or GH_TOKEN, COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN)

  # Additional LLM Providers
  AZURE_OPENAI_API_KEY       - Azure OpenAI models
  GROQ_API_KEY               - Groq models
  CEREBRAS_API_KEY           - Cerebras models
  XAI_API_KEY                - xAI Grok models
  OPENROUTER_API_KEY         - OpenRouter aggregated models
  KILO_API_KEY               - Kilo Gateway models
  MISTRAL_API_KEY            - Mistral models
  ZAI_API_KEY                - z.ai models (ZhipuAI/GLM)
  MINIMAX_API_KEY            - MiniMax models
  OPENCODE_API_KEY           - OpenCode Zen/OpenCode Go models
  CURSOR_ACCESS_TOKEN        - Cursor AI models
  AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY         - Vercel AI Gateway

  # Cloud Providers
  AWS_PROFILE                - AWS Bedrock (or AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID + AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY)
  GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT       - Google Vertex AI (requires GOOGLE_CLOUD_LOCATION)
  GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS - Service account for Vertex AI

  # Search & Tools
  EXA_API_KEY                - Exa web search
  BRAVE_API_KEY              - Brave web search
  PERPLEXITY_API_KEY         - Perplexity web search (API)
  PERPLEXITY_COOKIES         - Perplexity web search (session cookie)
  TAVILY_API_KEY             - Tavily web search
  ANTHROPIC_SEARCH_API_KEY   - Anthropic search provider

  # Configuration
  PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR        - Session storage directory (default: ~/.xcsh/agent)
  PI_PACKAGE_DIR             - Override package directory (for Nix/Guix store paths)
  PI_SMOL_MODEL              - Override smol/fast model (see --smol)
  PI_SLOW_MODEL              - Override slow/reasoning model (see --slow)
  PI_PLAN_MODEL              - Override planning model (see --plan)
  PI_NO_PTY                  - Disable PTY-based interactive bash execution

  For complete environment variable reference, see:
  docs/environment-variables.md
Available Tools (default-enabled unless noted):
  read          - Read file contents
  bash          - Execute bash commands
  edit          - Edit files with find/replace
  write         - Write files (creates/overwrites)
  grep          - Search file contents
  find          - Find files by glob pattern
  lsp           - Language server protocol (code intelligence)
  python        - Execute Python code (requires: xcsh setup python)
  notebook      - Edit Jupyter notebooks
  inspect_image - Analyze images with a vision model
  browser       - Browser automation (Puppeteer)
  task          - Launch sub-agents for parallel tasks
  todo_write    - Manage todo/task lists
  web_search    - Search the web
  ask           - Ask user questions (interactive mode only)

Sandbox Options:
  --no-sandbox               Disable the session filesystem discovery guard
  --allow-path <path>        Allow directory discovery at an additional path (repeatable)

Plugin Options:
  --plugin-dir <path>        Load plugin from directory (repeatable)

Useful Commands:
  xcsh agents unpack           - Export bundled subagents to ~/.xcsh/agent/agents (default)
  xcsh agents unpack --project - Export bundled subagents to ./.xcsh/agents

### validate --help
Validate manifests locally without API credentials

USAGE
  $ xcsh validate [FLAGS]

FLAGS
  -f, --filename=<value>     Manifest file, directory, or - for stdin
  -n, --namespace=<value>    Override the resource namespace
  -o, --output=<value>       Output format
  -R, --recursive            Read manifest directories recursively
      --result-file=<value>  Write the aggregate JSON report to a file

FLAGS

  -n, --namespace=<value>    Override the resource namespace
  -o, --output=<value>       Output format
  -R, --recursive            Read manifest directories recursively
      --result-file=<value>  Write the aggregate JSON report to a file

### create --help
Create resources from manifests and fail if they already exist

FLAGS
  -f, --filename=<value>     Manifest file, directory, or - for stdin
  -n, --namespace=<value>    Override the resource namespace
  -o, --output=<value>       Output format
  -R, --recursive            Read manifest directories recursively
      --result-file=<value>  Write the aggregate JSON report to a file
      --dry-run=<value>      Validate and calculate changes without mutation

Apply manifests by creating, updating, or preserving resources

  $ xcsh apply [FLAGS]

FLAGS
  -f, --filename=<value>     Manifest file, directory, or - for stdin
  -n, --namespace=<value>    Override the resource namespace
  -o, --output=<value>       Output format
  -R, --recursive            Read manifest directories recursively
      --result-file=<value>  Write the aggregate JSON report to a file
      --dry-run=<value>      Validate and calculate changes without mutation

### update --help
Update the xcsh executable or existing resources from manifests

USAGE
  $ xcsh update [FLAGS]

FLAGS
  -f, --filename=<value>     Manifest file, directory, or - for stdin
  -n, --namespace=<value>    Override the resource namespace
  -o, --output=<value>       Output format
  -R, --recursive            Read manifest directories recursively
      --result-file=<value>  Write the aggregate JSON report to a file
      --dry-run=<value>      Validate and calculate changes without mutation
      --force                Force executable update (short -f is reserved for resource manifests)
  -c, --check                Check for executable updates without installing

EXAMPLES
  xcsh update                         # update the executable
  xcsh update --check                 # check the executable version
  xcsh update --force                 # force an executable reinstall
  xcsh self-update -f                 # short force form for the executable
  xcsh update -f manifest.yaml        # update resources from a manifest

### get --help
Get or list live resources

USAGE
  $ xcsh get [KIND] [NAME] [FLAGS]

ARGUMENTS
  KIND   Resource kind
  NAME   Resource name

FLAGS
  -n, --namespace=<value>    Override the resource namespace
  -o, --output=<value>       Output format
      --result-file=<value>  Write the aggregate JSON report to a file
  -f, --filename=<value>     Manifest file, directory, or - for stdin
  -R, --recursive            Read manifest directories recursively

### export --help
Export live resources as manifests

USAGE
  $ xcsh export [KIND] [NAME] [FLAGS]

ARGUMENTS
  KIND   Resource kind
  NAME   Resource name

FLAGS
  -n, --namespace=<value>    Override the resource namespace
  -o, --output=<value>       Manifest output format
      --result-file=<value>  Write the aggregate JSON report to a file
      --all                  Export every supported resource kind
  -f, --file=<value>         Write formatted output to a file

### delete --help
Delete resources identified by manifests or kind and name

USAGE
  $ xcsh delete [KIND] [NAME] [FLAGS]

ARGUMENTS
  KIND   Resource kind
  NAME   Resource name

FLAGS
  -n, --namespace=<value>    Override the resource namespace
  -o, --output=<value>       Output format
      --result-file=<value>  Write the aggregate JSON report to a file
  -f, --filename=<value>     Manifest file, directory, or - for stdin
  -R, --recursive            Read manifest directories recursively
      --dry-run=<value>      Validate deletion without mutation

### config --help
Manage configuration settings

  $ xcsh config [ACTION] [KEY] [VALUE] [FLAGS]

ARGUMENTS
  ACTION   Config action (list|get|set|reset|path|init-xdg)
  KEY      Setting key
  VALUE    Value (for set/reset)

FLAGS
      --json  Output JSON

### setup --help
Install dependencies for optional features

USAGE
  $ xcsh setup [COMPONENT] [FLAGS]

ARGUMENTS
  COMPONENT   Component to install (python|stt|litellm)

FLAGS
  -c, --check  Check if dependencies are installed
      --json   Output status as JSON

### agents --help
Manage bundled task agents

USAGE
  $ xcsh agents [ACTION] [FLAGS]

ARGUMENTS
  ACTION   Agents action (unpack)

FLAGS
  -f, --force        Overwrite existing agent files
      --json         Output JSON
      --dir=<value>  Output directory (overrides --user/--project)
      --user         Write to ~/.xcsh/agent/agents (default)
      --project      Write to ./.xcsh/agents

EXAMPLES
  # Export bundled agents into user config (default)
    xcsh agents unpack
  # Export bundled agents into project config
    xcsh agents unpack --project
  # Overwrite existing local agent files
    xcsh agents unpack --project --force
  # Export into a custom directory
    xcsh agents unpack --dir ./tmp/agents --json

### plugin --help
Manage plugins (install, uninstall, list, etc.)

USAGE
  $ xcsh plugin [ACTION] [TARGETS] [FLAGS]

ARGUMENTS
  ACTION    Plugin action (install|uninstall|list|link|doctor|features|config|enable|disable|marketplace|discover|upgrade)
  TARGETS   Packages, paths, or plugin names

FLAGS
      --json             Output JSON
      --fix              Attempt to fix issues (doctor)
      --force            Force install
      --dry-run          Show actions without applying changes
  -l, --local            Operate on local plugin directory
      --enable=<value>   Enable a feature
      --disable=<value>  Disable a feature
      --set=<value>      Set plugin config (key=value)
      --scope=<value>    Install scope: "user" (default) or "project"

### worker --help
Run a headless extension-bridge worker (no TUI); blocks until SIGTERM

USAGE
  $ xcsh worker

Run the detached control server that spawns/reaps per-tab workers; blocks forever

### office --help
Serve, print, or sideload the embedded xcsh Office task pane

USAGE
  $ xcsh office [ACTION] [APP] [FLAGS]

ARGUMENTS
  ACTION   serve | manifest | sideload | recycle (serve|manifest|sideload|recycle)
  APP      Office app for sideload (excel | powerpoint | word) (excel|powerpoint|word)

FLAGS
  -o, --out=<value>  Write manifest.json to this path (manifest action)
